about: Check fixtures for the ladder step's code, and worked examples for engineers. Each answer passes the schema and checks 1 to 8. An event is answered in at most three outcomes (D409), the last written by code. `written` is a projection of what the step writes for it, not the whole record: the view's object, kind, year and due day, and each rung's position, label, condition and, for a figure, its bounds. The complete rows (every column of `views`, `rungs` and `clean_ladders`, the outcome record included) are DESIGN.md §5.4's, and the build tests them on these answers. They are NOT offered as sound ladders: whether a ladder is right is a reader's judgement, tested by the planted-fault dry runs; where a fixture has a `note`, it records what readers found in it. This file is never sent to the model; the request is candidate-system.txt, the payload followed by candidate-closing.txt, and the schema. The fixtures use stored theses of the covered company on purpose; the request itself names no company.

shape: a company's figure where the higher end is favourable (a made-up thesis; it shows the order of positions)

ladder.question: What same-store sales growth will the retailer report for its fiscal 2027?

figure.favourable_why: Faster same-store growth lifts revenue and margin on a fixed store base.

reference.words: management guided same-store sales growth to about 4%

rungs.label: Neutral
rungs.condition: from 3.5 percent to below 5 percent (the reference when the question opened: "management guided same-store sales growth to about 4%")

note: The answer lists its ranges out of order; code sorts them. Position 1 is always Strongly bullish: with the higher end favourable it holds the highest range, with the lower end favourable the lowest. Whole bounds are written as integers (5, 2), the others in plain decimal notation with no exponent and no trailing zeros (6.5, 3.5). The fixture runs with a test research list whose one company is the made-up ticker RTLR; the reference's words are in the fixture's article.

fixture_input.fiscal_year_note: RTLR's fiscal year ends in January: this year is FY2027, next year is FY2028.

thesis.description: What same-store sales growth will the retailer report for its fiscal 2027?
thesis.outcome: The retailer's fiscal 2027 same-store sales growth.
thesis.period: Fiscal 2027, at the annual results in March 2027.

item.title: Retailer lifts outlook after strong spring
item.text: The retailer raised its outlook on Monday after a strong spring season. For fiscal 2027, management guided same-store sales growth to about 4%, up from 3% before. Analysts said traffic gains were broad-based.
